text:
maria: quick heads-up — EU-west saw intermittent p99 token latency spikes after yesterday's rack powercap rollout. seems like GPUs on a subset of racks dropped into perf-limited mode and scheduler spilled slices into shared pools, which amplified noisy-tenant contention. logs below.

aj: saw the same. p50 fine, p95 small uptick, p99 jumped from ~30ms -> ~220ms for short chat requests. KV-cache hit-rate dropped 12%.

leo: digging — powercap caused some GPUs to throttle frequency. jobs evicted from those hosts because they missed our warmup TTL, scheduler moved them to other racks; once dedicated spare capacity exhausted it fell back to shared pool routing. that shared pool is already under higher multiplexing, so tail got hit.

priya: can we short-circuit fallback to shared pool for tenants with low cache-warmth? prefer region-local warm pool first, even if it means a small delay. also consider deferring routing decision when powercap events detected.

maria: agree. proposal: change fallback policy from immediate "fallback_to_shared=true" to "fallback_defer=30s, bias_by=cache_warmth_score". won't solve cost but should reduce tail amplification. also think about a temporary per-rack safety margin during known powercap windows.

aj: quick probe data:
```
2024-11-02T15:02:11Z gpu-rack-17 powercap=20W freq=1200MHz perf_state=throttled
2024-11-02T15:02:12Z scheduler evict tenant=acme-ux dest=shared-pool-2 reason=dedicated_full
2024-11-02T15:02:12Z kvcache tenant=acme-ux hit_rate=0.67 -> 0.58
```

leo: small fix we can try immediately: bump dedicated pool soft-threshold from 85% -> 92% for EU-west for next 1h to avoid spuriously spilling on transient throttling. that reduces chance of migration churn.

priya: cost note — keeping higher soft-threshold increases reserved capacity pressure and could raise monthly commit. but transient bump for 1h after infra changes seems okay. recommend ops signoff. :thumbsup:

ingrid: from cost-control side, alternative is short-term fractional slice credits for orgs that can't tolerate tail spikes. cheaper than reserving full extra slices, but requires routing awareness.

maria: patch I'm about to roll in eng-infra namespace (quick):
```
# bump soft threshold for eu-west dedicated pools
kubectl -n infra patch configmap pool-config --patch '{"data":{"eu_west_soft_threshold":"0.92","fallback_defer_secs":"30","bias_by":"cache_warmth"}}'
```

sre-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2024-157 (auto) — "eu-west powercap -> spillover -> tail latency". Pager duty: @sre-oncall.

aj: monitoring dashboards: added temporary p99 alert at 200ms and a kvcache-hit drop rule. will revert thresholds after 2h unless we see sustained shift.

leo: can someone add a tag on the affected racks so autoscaler avoids tight packing for next rolling maintenance? label: "powercap-rolled-2024-11-02"

maria: tagging now. thanks everyone. follow-ups: 1) confirm rollback plan if tail doesn't improve in 30m; 2) postmortem if pattern repeats after next infra change. :eyes:
